Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.action: Remove and destroy infected leaves. Apply copper-based bactericide spray every 7-10 days. Avoid overhead irrigation and working in wet fields to prevent spread.

Pepper__bell___healthy.action: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring.

Potato___Early_blight.action: Apply mancozeb or chlorothalonil spray. Remove infected lower leaves. Rotate crops next season to reduce soil-borne spores.

Potato___Late_blight.action: Apply systemic fungicide immediately. Destroy infected foliage. Avoid irrigation during humid weather and improve field drainage.

Potato___healthy.action: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.action: Apply copper-based bactericide. Remove infected plant debris. Avoid overhead watering and rotate crops.

Tomato_Early_blight.action: Remove affected lower leaves. Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb fungicide every 7-10 days. Avoid overhead watering.

Tomato_Late_blight.action: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately. Apply copper-based fungicide. Improve field drainage and spacing.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.action: Improve ventilation and reduce humidity around plants. Apply a suitable fungicide and avoid wetting leaves during watering.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.action: Remove infected lower leaves promptly. Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or copper-based) and avoid overhead irrigation.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.action: Spray with miticide or neem oil. Increase humidity around plants and remove heavily infested leaves. Check undersides of leaves regularly.

Tomato__Target_Spot.action: Apply fungicide (chlorothalonil or mancozeb). Remove infected leaves and improve air circulation between plants.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.action: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately — this spreads via whiteflies. Control whitefly population with sticky traps or insecticide. Use virus-resistant varieties next season.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.action: Remove and destroy infected plants — no cure exists. Disinfect tools between plants and wash hands after handling infected plants to prevent spread.

Tomato_healthy.action: No treatment needed. Continue regular monitoring.
